title: Working Holiday in Melbourne: Coffee, Culture, and Cafe Work
summary: Aki is a Japanese adult on a working holiday in Melbourne. He wants a cafe job, better English, and real coffee skills.

cover.alt: English lesson illustration for Working Holiday in Melbourne: Coffee, Culture, and Cafe Work

blocks.title: Introduction
paragraphs: Aki is a Japanese adult on a working holiday in Melbourne. He wants a cafe job, better English, and real coffee skills. Before his first shift, he needs to understand his visa, his workplace rights, Melbourne coffee culture, and clear cafe communication.

items.prompt: What would you like to learn in a Melbourne cafe?
What may feel different when you work in another country?
Which is harder: speaking to a manager or taking a customer order?

blocks.title: Step 1: Check Before You Start
paragraphs: A working holiday lets a young adult travel and work in Australia for a time. Aki must check his own current visa conditions before he accepts a job. He should use the official Home Affairs website because conditions can change. Aki also checks the job. Is he an employee? Is it a casual job with changing hours? What is the pay, and when will he work? In Australia, migrant workers have the same workplace rights and protections as other employees. Aki should keep a record of his hours and receive a pay slip after he is paid. For exact current information, he can use the official Fair Work tools.

images.alt: English lesson illustration for Working Holiday in Melbourne: Coffee, Culture, and Cafe Work scene 1: Step 1: Check Before You Start

items.prompt: What two official places can Aki check?
items.answer: He can check Home Affairs for his visa and Fair Work for workplace information.
items.explanation:
I would ask about __ first because __.

blocks.title: Useful Phrases
paragraphs: Could I check my roster and shift time?

blocks.title: Step 2: Learn Melbourne Coffee Culture
paragraphs: Coffee is an important part of social life in Melbourne. Italian migration after World War II helped espresso culture grow in the city. Today, people often meet in cafes or buy coffee before work. A regular customer may visit the same cafe many times. A barista makes coffee drinks. The barista uses a grinder for the beans and steam for the milk. Milk texture means how the warm milk and foam feel. A flat white is a popular espresso-and-milk drink, but each cafe can have its own recipe and work method. Aki should watch, ask, and practise instead of guessing.

images.alt: English lesson illustration for Working Holiday in Melbourne: Coffee, Culture, and Cafe Work scene 2: Step 2: Learn Melbourne Coffee Culture

items.prompt: Why should Aki learn the cafe's own method?
items.answer: Cafes can make drinks and organise work in different ways.

blocks.title: Step 3: Communicate on Your First Shift
paragraphs: On his first shift, Aki has training. Training is time to learn the job. A manager may show him the coffee machine, food-safety rules, cleaning jobs, and the order system. Required meetings and training are work time. If a cafe asks for a trial shift, Aki should check the details and use Fair Work information rather than assume it is unpaid. Australian speech can sound relaxed. Coworkers may use first names, and some people say mate. However, not everyone speaks in the same way. Friendly language does not change workplace rules. When Aki does not understand, he can clarify: ask a short question, repeat the instruction, and confirm the next action.

images.alt: English lesson illustration for Working Holiday in Melbourne: Coffee, Culture, and Cafe Work scene 3: Step 3: Communicate on Your First Shift

items.prompt: What can Aki do when an instruction is not clear?
items.answer: He can ask, repeat the instruction, and confirm the next action.

blocks.title: Step 4: Check the Order and Fix Problems
paragraphs: Cafe English is often short and polite. Aki checks the drink, size, and milk before he starts. Then he repeats the order. This gives the customer time to correct a detail. Mistakes can still happen. Aki may hear the wrong size or use the wrong milk. He should stay calm, apologise, and explain the next action. Good service is not only fast. It is also careful and clear. A customer usually feels better when the worker notices a problem and fixes it politely.

images.alt: English lesson illustration for Working Holiday in Melbourne: Coffee, Culture, and Cafe Work scene 4: Step 4: Check the Order and Fix Problems

items.prompt: What three details should Aki check?
items.answer: He should check the drink, size, and milk.

blocks.title: Useful Phrases
paragraphs: What size would you like?

blocks.title: Useful Speaking Patterns
paragraphs:
- Could I check my roster and shift time?
- How will I receive my pay slip?
- Could you show me that again, please?
- What size would you like?
- Let me check your order.
- Sorry about that. I will fix it now.

turns.speaker: Manager
turns.text: Hi, Aki. Your training starts at nine tomorrow.

turns.speaker: Aki
turns.text: Thanks. Could I check my shift time and the rest of the roster?

turns.speaker: Manager
turns.text: Of course. I will send the roster this afternoon.

turns.speaker: Aki
turns.text: Great. How will I receive my pay slip?

turns.speaker: Manager
turns.text: It will be online. I will show you after training.

turns.speaker: Aki
turns.text: Thank you. That makes everything clear.

turns.speaker: Aki
turns.text: See you tomorrow. Have a good afternoon.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Hi. Could I have a small flat white with soy milk?

turns.speaker: Aki
turns.text: One small flat white with soy milk. Is that right?

turns.speaker: Aki
turns.text: Sorry, I picked up regular milk. I will remake it with soy milk now.

turns.speaker: Aki
turns.text: Here you are. Thanks for waiting, and enjoy your coffee.

items.prompt: Choose one roleplay. Change one detail, such as the shift time, drink size, or milk. Practise the new conversation with a partner.

blocks.title: Final Reflection
paragraphs: Aki can enjoy Melbourne coffee culture and protect himself at work when he checks official information, asks clear questions, and practises the cafe's method. Imagine tomorrow is your first shift abroad. What is one question you will ask your manager, and why?
